chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan who said, 'Ayoub, brother of Adeym, narrated to me from the Sheikh, who said to me, my father (peace be upon him) said:'

'Whenever you face the water spout, say: O Allah! Emancipate my neck from the Fire, and expand upon me from Your permissible sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the wicked ones of the Jinn and the humans, and enter me into Paradise by Your mercy.'

key_terms.الْمِيزَابُ: The water spout of the Kaaba, a specific point of focus during Tawaf
key_terms.فَسَقَةِ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ: The wicked/transgressors among the Jinn and humans

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication when facing the water spout of the Kaaba during pilgrimage?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of al-Saduq’s contemporaries, this narration highlights the specific devotional practice of facing the Kaaba’s water spout (mizab) during Tawaf, a spot traditionally associated with the acceptance of prayers. The supplication encapsulates core Shia theological concerns, linking physical ritual with spiritual liberation from Hellfire and protection from the unseen evils of Jinn and humans, ultimately relying on divine mercy for entry into Paradise.
